newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian royalist troops claim advances.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalist troops claim advances.

text.p: Forces loyal to Cambodia's ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh have made advances against troops under strongman Hun Sen in the north, one of Ranariddh's officers said on Thursday.
The officer said Hun Sen's forces were unable to bring up reinforcements as royalist troops had blown up bridges on the road linking the north to central Cambodia.
Royalist forces had taken the town of Samrong and pushed south, forcing Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's troops to withdraw, but Khmer Rouge guerrillas later looted the town, he said.
"We now control the area for nearly 100 km (60 miles) from the Thai border, down to Samrong and beyond," the officer, Colonel Saing Chhay Mony, told Reuters.

There was no independent confirmation of the claim. There have been conflicting reports over who is in control of Samrong, 330 km (200 miles) northwest of Phnom Penh and 30 km (20 miles) from the Thai border, over recent days.
Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh in a bloody coup on July 6 after driving the prince's forces from Phnom Penh.
A Cambodian army officer loyal to Hun Sen confirmed earlier this week that government forces had been pushed back from Samrong.
The officer said royalist forces were being helped by Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
But in Phnom Penh, a government spokesman said Hun Sen's forces were meeting little opposition from the royalist troops and denied that royalist forces were still in Samrong.
A news photographer who was in Samrong early on Wednesday said Hun Sen's troops were in control of the town although intermittent shelling in the area continued.
Saing Chhay Mony said between 200 and 300 Khmer Rouge guerrillas had looted Samrong after royalist forces had retaken the town and pushed on beyond it.
"They robbed and looted people and turned Samrong into a ghost town," the royalist officer said.
A Thai army officer on the border confirmed that soldiers had looted Samrong but said he did not know which faction the soldiers came from.
Thousands of civilians have fled the area of fighting, many heading for Thailand.
Thai authorities estimated about 20,000 Cambodians were waiting at the border and said they would be allowed to cross to Thai soil if the fighting worsened.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees said on Tuesday it was concerned that Thailand was not allowing civilians to cross into Thailand and that the UNHCR was not being allowed into the area.
Cambodia was to have joined the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Wednesday, but the group postponed its admission after Ranariddh's overthrow.

Hun Sen originally rejected ASEAN's efforts to mediate in the political crisis. But Foreign Minister Ung Huot, named by Hun Sen to replace Ranariddh, told ASEAN ministers meeting in Malaysia on Wednesday Hun Sen had changed his mind and was willing to accept mediation.
